title: NATO Bucharest summit declines Membership Action Plan for Georgia and Ukraine
body:
At the NATO summit in Bucharest on 3 April 2008 the allies did not grant Georgia or Ukraine a Membership Action Plan (MAP). The decision followed a dispute that became visible on 2 April. The United States, Canada, Poland, Romania, the Czech Republic and the Baltic states strongly backed MAP for both countries, while Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Belgium opposed it. Despite urging from US President George W. Bush, France and Germany blocked both applications. Germany's position reflected its interest in reconciliation with Russia and its dependence on Russian gas, and concerns about governance and corruption in both candidate countries were also raised.

The summit declaration nonetheless stated that NATO welcomed Ukraine's and Georgia's Euro-Atlantic aspirations for membership and that "these countries will become members of NATO". It described MAP as the next step toward membership, said the allies supported the two countries' applications for MAP, and promised a review in December 2008.

Georgia welcomed the outcome and called it a historic success. Britain supported both countries but thought the timing of their accession should remain open. Russian leader Vladimir Putin later said he was pleased that Georgia and Ukraine had not been invited to MAP, at least for the time being. The wording, a promise of eventual membership without a concrete path, is often cited in accounts of the lead-up to the August 2008 war.
